title: Generative Next POI Recommendation with Semantic ID

problem.claim: POI recommendation systems aim to predict users' next destinations from their preferences and historical check-ins.

gap.claim: Existing generative POI recommendation methods commonly use random numeric POI IDs, which limits modeling semantic relationships between similar locations.

contributions.claim: GNPR-SID introduces a semantic POI ID representation method for an LLM-based generative next-POI recommendation model.

The method combines a Semantic ID Construction module based on semantic and collaborative features with a Generative POI Recommendation module that fine-tunes LLMs to predict the next POI using semantic IDs.
The method constructs semantic IDs using residual-quantized variational autoencoder POI quantization and a diversity loss that encourages uniform distribution across the semantic space.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the semantic POI ID representation method as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report improved recommendation accuracy and model generalization from incorporating user interaction patterns and POI semantic features into semantic ID generation.
The authors report that experiments on three benchmark datasets show GNPR-SID substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods, with up to 16% improvement in recommendation accuracy.

narrative_sequence.summary: The task is predicting users' next destinations from preferences and historical check-ins.
Random numeric POI IDs limit semantic modeling of relationships between similar locations.
GNPR-SID introduces semantic POI IDs for an LLM-based generative recommendation model.
The system constructs semantic IDs from semantic and collaborative features, quantizes POIs into a discrete semantic space, applies diversity loss, and fine-tunes LLMs to predict the next POI.
Experiments on three benchmark datasets are reported to show up to 16% higher recommendation accuracy than state-of-the-art methods.

source_observation.claim: The method incorporates semantic and collaborative features into POI identifiers and uses those identifiers for generative prediction.

interpretation.claim: Representations that encode both item meaning and interaction structure may help generative recommenders model similarity and user behavior together.

application.claim: For another sequential recommendation task, consider constructing item representations from content and interaction signals before using them as generation targets.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach transfers beyond POI recommendation or which feature types are necessary for the reported gains.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three benchmark datasets.
The abstract does not provide baseline identities, evaluation protocol, or statistical significance.
The abstract does not quantify the contribution of the semantic ID construction, quantization, or diversity loss components separately.
The abstract does not report computational cost, training details, or reproducibility information.
